name: Archive permitted email attachments in Folderit and verify uploads

nodes.name: Setup: Archive email attachments in Folderit

parameters.content:
# Archive email attachments in Folderit
For a document intake mailbox. Splits every permitted attachment into its own item, preserves its binary data, uploads it and reads it back to check the stored name and folder.

1. Install **n8n-nodes-folderit 0.4.0 or later**. [Setup guide](https://www.folderit.com/knowledge-base/connect-folderit-to-n8n/)
2. In **New email with attachments**, create/select an IMAP credential with TLS and enter your intake mailbox. Follow your mail provider's app-password/OAuth requirements.
3. Open **Settings** and replace both UIDs; edit the allowed extensions.
4. Select a **Folderit OAuth2 API** credential in both Folderit nodes. The API client needs upload and read access to that destination.
5. Test with one small synthetic attachment and confirm its contents in Folderit before publishing/activating.

# Processing and recovery
No permitted attachments: no upload and no output. Multiple permitted attachments: one upload per file. Folderit rejects empty files and files over 100 MiB. Extension filtering is not malware detection.

The IMAP cursor tracks new messages; the template leaves read/unread status unchanged. Existing unseen messages may be fetched on first activation: use a dedicated, empty intake mailbox for the first test.

Uploads are not automatically retried. A failed execution can leave earlier attachments uploaded; the email cursor is not an archive receipt. Inspect execution history and the destination before retrying, then recover only missing attachments. Replaying a message can create duplicates. Add a durable business ledger if duplicate-free processing is required.

This template contains no saved credentials or pinned data. IMAP-to-Folderit delivery still needs validation with your mail provider.
